sources.title: Chakán Putum
sources.note: Infobox 1441-1529, capital Chakan Putum (modern Champotón); Spaniards battled the Maya in 1518 and 1519 and invaded between 1527 and 1528.

notes: NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no row for this province; Later Mayan City-States (1429-1546, 135,136 to 187,745 km2) covers the whole northern lowlands and contains it. The Kuchkabal page says the extent of the provinces 'is still debated' and that scholars disagree 'on whether they were territorial units or jurisdictions'; the shape here is a disc around the capital, soft, and no frontier is claimed. Cliopatria keeps its envelope to 1546 although the Spanish took the provinces one by one from 1527. CHAKAN PUTUM. Called 'Chanputun (Champotón)' on the conquest page; distinct from Chakan (Ti'ho, Mérida). The page puts the Tabasco peoples to its southwest; the Chontal Acalan province has no dossier.
